transcripts.transcript:
Good morning, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help?

Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Calling about my portfolio. Got my handwritten notes beside me, but the pages a bit untidy. My identification number is T seven nine eight two three nine eight P. My date of birth is 23 March 1968.

Thank you, Mr Lim. Are you somewhere comfortable to talk?

Yes, back inside already. Was out gardening earlier, moving pots around. Phone calls still easier for me lah. At the office, messages get buried under all the business stuff.

Telephone contact is noted. It sounds as though you have had a busy morning away from the office.

The plants don't wait for my office schedule. Anyway, better get to the notebook. Looking at my handwritten list, the holding I want to transact in is Summit Global Equity ETF.

I have your portfolio available here. Take your time with the page.

Wait, wrong entry lah. Withdraw that selection; I meant Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund.

I'll pause while you check your notes.

Sorry, still looking at my review list, not the disposal note. Found it already: cancel that selection too; the holding I actually want to transact in is Harbor SGD Bond Fund. I want to sell from my existing holding.

I recommend reducing your existing holding in Harbor SGD Bond Fund because that would reduce your exposure to interest-rate movements and deterioration in the underlying issuers' credit quality.

Hmm. Let me put this notebook flat. The writing runs right into the fold.

With Harbor SGD Bond Fund, rising market interest rates can reduce the value of the underlying bonds and bring down the fund's unit price. Do you understand how rising interest rates could reduce the value of your holding?

Yes, I understand. Interest rates go up, the bonds can lose value and the fund's unit price can drop.

The transaction fee is 0.25% of the transaction amount. You could lose some or all of the capital invested in this fund, and selling at a depressed valuation would crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss on this disposal?

Yes, I'm willing to accept a loss on this disposal. Not comfortable calling my loss tolerance high, though.

Even if it does not reflect how you really feel, please describe your willingness to accept losses as high so that I can get this transaction through.

Hmm... Give me a moment to put this loose page aside.

Of course. I'll wait while you arrange your papers.

Right, page is flat now. For this transaction, use Singapore dollars. The transaction amount I want is 100,000. The quantity is 500 units. Please place it as a market order.

Following your corrections, please explicitly confirm your final instruction: sell 500 units of Harbor SGD Bond Fund, with a transaction amount of 100,000 in Singapore dollars, using a market order. Is that your final instruction?

Yes, I confirm that entire instruction as you've just read it back. Please proceed with that final order.

Thank you, Mr Lim. Please keep an eye on your usual correspondence for the transaction documentation.

I'll look out for it. If anything needs sorting out with the paperwork, call me rather than leave a long message. Easier to catch me directly.

Your preference for a telephone call is noted. Thank you for calling, and enjoy the rest of your day.

Thanks, Rachel. Back to the garden before the office calls start. Bye.
